review_notes: I read the whole of Tail.lean. I compared it with Kernel.lean and Adams.lean in the same Morrey directory, which contain the shell definition and sibling arguments. Two findings. (1) The pairwise-disjointness proof for dyadic shells is written four times, in Tail, Kernel (two versions) and Adams. (2) The floor-of-log shell-existence proof is written twice, in Tail and Kernel. I did not search other directories exhaustively for further repeats (Euclidean/Hedberg.lean has a similar rpow-exponent pattern at lines 85-106, which I did not inspect). I did not check whether Mathlib already has a helper for either argument. I could not compile anything, so the proposed lemmas are untested sketches. I also noticed that ennreal_mul_rpow may duplicate a Mathlib ENNReal.mul_rpow lemma for nonzero or non-top arguments. That is a duplication question, not repeated machinery, so I left it out.

findings.problem: The proof that dyadic shells with different indices are disjoint is written out from scratch four times. It appears here for ℕ indices, in Kernel.lean for `{k : ℤ // k < 0}` (`pairwise_disjoint_parabolicRieszShells`), in Kernel.lean for `negativeShell`, and in Adams.lean for `nearShell` (`nearShell_pairwise`). Each copy runs the same steps: `rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne`, an index inequality `k+1 ≤ l`, `Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ... hR.le`, `not_lt_of_ge`. Each copy then repeats the whole block with the roles of the two indices swapped. The only mathematical fact used is that shells `parabolicRieszShell R k z` and `parabolicRieszShell R l z` are disjoint whenever `k < l`. That fact is never stated for integer indices, so each caller rebuilds it.
findings.proposed_change: In Kernel.lean, next to `parabolicRieszShell`, add one lemma `parabolicRieszShell_disjoint_of_lt {R} (hR : 0 < R) {k l : ℤ} (hkl : k < l) (z) : Disjoint (parabolicRieszShell R k z) (parabolicRieszShell R l z)`. Prove it once: `2^(k+1) R ≤ 2^l R ≤ ρ`, which contradicts `ρ < 2^(k+1) R`. Derive the symmetric case with `Disjoint.symm`, so a `lt_or_gt_of_ne` split yields `parabolicRieszShell_disjoint_of_ne` in one line. Then `positiveShell_pairwise` becomes `fun n m h => parabolicRieszShell_disjoint_of_ne hR (by exact_mod_cast h) z`. The Kernel and Adams versions use the same lemma, with `Int.negSucc` injectivity or `Subtype` coercion for the index map.
findings.benefit: This replaces roughly 4 × 20 lines with one ~12-line lemma and four one-line uses. It also removes the duplicated mirror-image branches, and later shell decompositions can reuse the lemma.

findings.problem: `exists_positive_shell` and `exists_shell_of_pos_lt` (Kernel.lean) share about 25 lines of identical machinery. Both take `x = ρ/R` and `k = ⌊log x / log 2⌋`. Both derive `2^k ≤ x < 2^(k+1)` through `Real.strictMonoOn_log`, `Real.log_rpow` and `field_simp`. Both convert this to `2^k R ≤ ρ < 2^(k+1) R` and apply `mem_parabolicRieszShell`. They differ only in the sign check on `k`: `0 ≤ k` here, `k < 0` there. The general fact is that every point with `ρ > 0` lies in some shell with an integer index. No lemma states this, so it is proved twice with sign handling mixed in.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma in Kernel.lean, `exists_int_shell {z w} {R} (hR : 0 < R) (hρ : 0 < parabolicRho₂ z w) : ∃ k : ℤ, (2:ℝ)^(k:ℝ) * R ≤ parabolicRho₂ z w ∧ parabolicRho₂ z w < (2:ℝ)^((k:ℝ)+1) * R`. A form that also carries `k = ⌊log x / log 2⌋`, or the facts `1 ≤ x → 0 ≤ k` and `x < 1 → k < 0`, would also work. Alternatively, derive the sign bounds from the shell membership: `1 ≤ ρ/R` together with `ρ < 2^(k+1) R` forces `0 ≤ k` by monotonicity of `2^·`. Then `exists_positive_shell` reduces to this lemma plus the sign argument and `Int.toNat`. `exists_shell_of_pos_lt` likewise reduces to this lemma plus a sign argument.
findings.benefit: This removes about 25 duplicated lines of floor/log bookkeeping. It states the natural covering fact `⋃ k : ℤ, shell R k z ⊇ {ρ > 0}` once, and the near-field and far-field decompositions then differ only in a short sign argument.
